instructions: In a large bowl, whisk the semolina, yogurt, salt and 3/4 cup water until smooth. Let it rest for 20 minutes while the semolina swells.
Meanwhile, finely chop 2 tbsp of the onion, 2 tbsp of the tomato and 2 tbsp of the cilantro. Grate 1/2 tsp of the ginger.
Stir the onion, tomato, cilantro and ginger into the batter. It should be thick but pourable. If it's too thick, stir in up to 1/4 cup of water.
Heat a large nonstick pan over medium heat and brush it lightly with oil.
Pour a scant 1/3 cup of batter into the pan and spread it into a thick round about 5 inches wide. Drizzle 1/2 tsp oil around the edge.
Cover and cook for 2 minutes, until the top looks set.
Flip it, press gently with a spatula and cook for 1 minute, until golden on both sides. Transfer to a plate and repeat with the rest of the batter. You should get about 6 cheelas.
Serve hot with the green chutney.
method_notes: Hebbar's Kitchen (the lead, 5 from 262) whisks the semolina with yogurt, rests it 20 minutes, then adds onion, tomato, ginger and cilantro. YummyTummy Aarthi's version blends the batter and adds grated carrot and spices (only one rating). Written as the lead has it, with its green chili left out to keep it mild. The 20 minute rest runs while you chop, and cooking takes about 18 minutes in one pan.
